methods.label: Match the contacting circumferences
methods.explanation:
Use the recorded interpretation that rolling is without slipping and that the same material point on each circle must be in contact at the beginning and end. A circle has positive radius, so the allowed integers satisfy \(1\le r<100\).

Track the contacting point along each circle's rim. Without slipping, equal arc lengths on the two rims are brought into contact. During one circuit, the contact travels once around circle \(A\), covering length \(2\pi\cdot100=200\pi\). Since circle \(B\)'s circumference is \(2\pi r\), the contact makes
\[
\frac{200\pi}{2\pi r}=\frac{100}{r}
\]
trips around its rim. The same material point on \(B\) returns to contact exactly when this number is an integer. The contact on \(A\) already returns after its one full lap. Thus precisely the positive divisors of 100 below 100 work.

To list all divisors, list factor pairs. The smaller factor in a pair is at most 10; checking the integers from 1 through 10 gives exactly
\[
1\cdot100,
\quad2\cdot50,
\quad4\cdot25,
\quad5\cdot20,
\quad10\cdot10.
\]
These pairs include every divisor. Counting 10 only once and excluding 100 leaves
\[
1,2,4,5,10,20,25,50.
\]
Each makes \(100/r\) an integer and therefore satisfies the return condition. Under the stated interpretation, there are \(8\) possible radii, choice B.
methods.levelReason: The proof matches equal contact-arc lengths and exhaustively lists factor pairs of 100. It requires neither a rotation formula nor a prime-exponent divisor-count formula.
